orders: Observe the patient walking while distracted (for example, counting backward) and then walking while pretending to kick a ball.
Perform the straight-leg-raise and Hoover sign tests for functional leg weakness.
Test tandem gait, heel walking, and toe walking.
Perform a Romberg test and a pull test for postural instability.
MRI of the brain with and without contrast.
MRI of the cervical and thoracic spine with and without contrast.
Serum ceruloplasmin, serum copper, 24-hour urinary copper, liver function tests, and slit-lamp examination for Kayser–Fleischer rings.
Neurologic examination specifically documenting blepharospasm, oromandibular dystonia, cervical dystonia, and task-specific axial dystonia.
served: gait observation including turning and doorways
eyelid function (apraxia of lid opening, blepharospasm, lid retraction)
trunk posture: lateral flexion (Pisa) and antecollis, standing versus supine
